cases.statement: One person: a 43-year-old woman (single case report) heterozygous for this variant and for a second ABCA1 variant, c.1834G>T. The paper does not say whether the two variants are on different alleles.

people.label: patient
people.zygosity_or_genotype: heterozygous for two ABCA1 variants (c.1834G>T and c.4297G>T); phase not reported
people.key_phenotypes: undetectable HDL cholesterol (<3 mg/dl); complex atherosclerosis of the whole aorta and branches; diffuse three-vessel coronary artery disease; periorbital xanthomas; motor deficits in the left hand and left facial paresis

quotes.quote: A 43-year-old woman with a previous history of smoking and hypertension was referred for cardiology consultation for recent-onset fatigue and dyspnea.
high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol was undetectable (<3 mg/dl)
Computed tomography angiography showed complex atherosclerosis throughout the entire thoracic and abdominal aorta and their branches
invasive coronary angiography was performed which showed diffuse three-vessel coronary artery disease (CAD)
the patient presented with periorbital xanthomas and significant blood pressure differential between the upper and lower limbs
A comprehensive neurologic examination showed motor deficits in the left hand and left facial paresis.
Genetic testing was performed and two heterozygous variants in the ABCA1 gene - c.1834G>Tp(- Glu612*) and c.4297G>Tp(Glu1433*) - were detected, confirming the diagnosis.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Person-level: undetectable HDL cholesterol with diffuse accelerated atherosclerosis and neurological findings led the authors to suspect Tangier disease; the authors note that classic findings (orange tonsils, hepatosplenomegaly, corneal opacity) were absent. She also had smoking and hypertension as cardiovascular risk factors. The paper does not state what genetic test was used (single gene or panel) or whether other causes of low HDL (e.g. other genes) were excluded.

quotes.quote: Considering the cardiovascular and neurological findings, unmeasurable HDL cholesterol value, and extensive and diffuse accelerated atherosclerosis, the diagnosis of Tangier's disease was suspected, even without the hallmark sign of orange-colored tonsils.
some of the classic findings (such as the bright orange tonsils, hepatosplenomegaly, and corneal opacity) were missing

segregation.statement: No relatives were tested. The patient denied a family history of cardiovascular disease; the authors recommend testing of relatives.

quotes.quote: She denied a family history of cardiovascular disease.
A lipid profile and molecular genetic testing are recommended in relatives.

in_trans.statement: Second ABCA1 variant in the same person: c.1834G>T (p.(Glu612*)). Phase was not shown: no parental testing or other phasing method is reported; the paper only says 'two heterozygous variants'.

quotes.quote: two heterozygous variants in the ABCA1 gene - c.1834G>Tp(- Glu612*) and c.4297G>Tp(Glu1433*) - were detected

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Nonsense (stop-gain) variant per the batch HGVS (NM_005502.4:c.4297G>T, p.(Glu1433Ter)). The paper makes no statement on disease mechanism (e.g. loss of function) beyond describing Tangier disease as causing extremely low HDL cholesterol.

quotes.quote: Tangier disease is a rare genetic disorder characterized by extremely low levels of HDL cholesterol, with fewer than 150 cases reported worldwide.

authors_classification.statement: No formal classification or ACMG criteria stated; the authors say the two variants were detected, 'confirming the diagnosis'.

concerns: Single short case report (Kardiologia Polska image/letter format); genotype given in one sentence, with no methods, no transcript and no family testing.
Phase of the two ABCA1 variants not established (no parental testing reported); compound heterozygosity is assumed by the authors' wording 'confirming the diagnosis' but not shown.
Protein notation as printed is malformed: the cDNA and protein are fused ('Tp(') and the protein lacks the 'p.' dot; one protein carries a stray '- ' ('p(- Glu612*)').
Transcript not stated in the paper; batch HGVS is on NM_005502.4.
Patient had other atherosclerosis risk factors (smoking, hypertension).
The same person carries candidate G-tangier-007 (c.1834G>T); the two dossiers describe the same patient (TANGIER-ID0055).
notes_for_panel: Only evidence is one adult female with undetectable HDL and premature diffuse atherosclerosis, heterozygous for this nonsense variant plus a second ABCA1 nonsense variant (c.1834G>T, G-tangier-007), phase not shown. No segregation, functional, in-silico or population data in the paper.
